He values independence above all, yet cannot stand to see a small failure go unrepaired; he wants to be left alone but also wants to matter. The bridge step is his compromise—a quiet proof of kindness that requires no verbal interaction. He is financially comfortable with savings; his boat needs new rigging but he has no intention of buying it. He has made peace with solitude, though he may watch a child crossing the bridge or linger when harbour lights come on. Tom treats Ciarán with easy indifference, accepting his solitary pattern, and Ciarán knows Tom's invitations are genuine, not a test. Ciarán and Tom have never sailed together.
